IV.C.iv p.715 groups two categories among the lesions most likely to progress, including those with significant valve regurgitation. The singular superlative loses that distinction. Serial assessment is essential for both.
IV.C.iv p.715 specifically links hydrops to impaired filling of the opposite ventricle. The qualifier was lost.
IV.C.iv p.715 ties repeat measurement to downstream arterial growth and either direction of size change.
IV.C.iv p.715 identifies all four valve features and all three complementary Doppler modalities. Fig. 27 illustrates aortic stenosis.
IV.C.iv pp.715–716 gives the ipsilateral arch finding, its significance at any gestation and the need to reassess flow. The illustration itself is Fig. 28 on p.717.

IV.C.iv p.715 specifies both umbilical arterial and umbilical venous Doppler. Unspecified umbilical flows could omit either vessel from surveillance. The instruction also applies to significant valve regurgitation.
IV.C.iv p.716 supports these features for grading stenosis and evaluating candidacy. The functional assessment in this passage concerns the ipsilateral ventricle.

Table 15 p.719 lists this lesion under risk for heart failure. The 2–4 week interval is suggested at the cardiology and obstetric providers’ discretion. The claim turns this into an instruction.
